newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING sees Brazil power stocks boosted by rate rise.
newsitem.headline: ING sees Brazil power stocks boosted by rate rise.

text.p: ING Barings said this week's average 9.92 percent rise in Brazil's electrical rates would help boost local power stock prices to those of peers in Chile and Peru.
"The news is positive for the sector and should help propel share-price valuations higher to approach the range of utilities in neighboring Chile and Peru," ING said in a research report.
"In this context, we continue to see a 20-30 percent upside to year-end for major stocks in the sector."
The investment bank said its top picks among Brazilian are Copel while profit-takers should consider Cesp and Cemig, it added.

ING Barings said the firms benefitting the most from the tariff rise are Eletrobras, by way of its generating units Furnas and Eletrosul; integrated firms Copel and Cemig; and some distributing companies.

The bank said it will adjust earnings estimates for several stocks, but only Eletrobras and Copel forecasts will see significant changes "due to the higher than the expected increase in the generation tariff."
"We expect to raise estimates for Eletrobras," it said.
The latest rate rise, the first since November 1995, took affect on Tuesday, but will be reflected in company revenues starting only in May due to a lag in billing, it added.
